entries.title: Aaron Shapiro — Respect the House
entries.teaser: Shap's Almanac profile spans the house, the casino, and a remarkably complete history.
body: The 2024 Almanac presents Shap as a steady early-era contender: a 2014 finalist, a 2015 Saunders survivor, and a manager whose weekly highs and lows were often more dramatic than his final record.

The profile traces Shap's later playoff returns, his head-to-head balance across the league, and his VPC service. The narrative is preserved as Almanac context; season records, scores, and finishes remain canonical JSON facts.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 3–5; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Matt Singer — The Lawn and the Relay
entries.teaser: Singer's Almanac profile mixes draft-room lore with a dominant run.
body: The Almanac records Singer's lawn-drinking explanation for missing the inaugural draft, then follows the return, the 2016 title, and the 2017 relay-era personality. It treats the lawn story as draft-weekend lore, not a punishment.

The profile also reviews Singer's VPC role, mind games, strong single-season records, and later playoff turns. These are narrative context through the 2024 edition, while all displayed numerical outcomes are selected from the repository's canonical season data.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 5–8; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Dillon Nussbaum — The Mic
entries.teaser: Nuss's profile is a long arc of records, rivalry, and stand-up punishment.
body: The Almanac follows Nuss from an early Saunders appearance through a sustained playoff presence, a close 2020 season, and the 42.00 low-score record. His rivalry with Rishi and repeated strategic choices are part of the league's running history.

The profile closes on Nuss fulfilling the virtual stand-up punishment and on the difference between a memorable anecdote and a measured result. The entry keeps that context searchable without replacing the canonical record or score tables.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 8–11; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Ian Plotnick — The Breakthrough
entries.teaser: Plot's profile tracks the long route to a first playoff breakthrough.
body: The Almanac describes Plotnick's early near-misses, eventual 2018 playoff breakthrough, and the rivalries and trades that shaped the middle years. It gives the league a narrative record of persistence rather than a new statistical source.
Trade anecdotes and the later administrative handoff are retained as reviewed context. Any score, standing, draft slot, or title shown beside this entry must be read from canonical repository assets.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 11–14; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Rishi Patel — The Keys
entries.teaser: Rishi's profile is built around hidden keys, rivalries, and a late breakthrough.
body: The Almanac frames Rishi's career through the hidden-keys motif, the long rivalry with Shap, the 2021 turnaround, and the restoration of dignity to the Saunders position through an in-person punishment. It also records his place in the most lopsided rivalry described by the edition.
This is reviewed league context through 2024. The interface continues to derive records, points, playoff finishes, and championship margins from canonical data rather than from this prose.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 21–24; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Michael Zuckerman — The Mahomes Era
entries.teaser: Zook's Almanac profile covers balance, titles, and a run of bold management choices.
body: The Almanac presents Zook as a balanced opponent with a 2018 points explosion, several playoff successes, and a strategy of riding a single team across multiple seasons. It also recounts draft-competition dominance and the management decisions that ended later playoff runs.

The profile is intentionally narrative: the current site retains the canonical champion, Saunders, record, and points values in its data assets and uses this entry only for the reviewed story around them.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 24–27; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Joel Denicoff — Often Imitated
entries.teaser: Joel's profile covers the elevator ride, title defenses, and commissioner years.
body: The Almanac follows Joel from the early championship years through an improbable worst-to-first turn, later title-defense pressure, and the head-to-head records that made his two postseason runs distinctive. It preserves the supplied imitation line as personality, not as a claim about copied work.

Joel's commissioner service is described as a transition-era role with shared boundary years. The administrative summary remains separate from season statistics and does not infer exclusive tenure from the displayed range.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 27–31; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Joe Haynes — The Original Commissioner
entries.teaser: Joe's profile closes the Almanac with early titles and the first administration.
body: The Almanac describes Haynes as the initial commissioner, organizer of the early league, and a two-time top-seed owner whose title and Saunders runs anchor the opening years. It also notes the later return to strong form and the narrow all-time wins gap.
The profile is a reviewed 2024 narrative reference. The site's standings, title counts, records, and finishes continue to come from canonical season summaries and game history.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 31–34; numbers remain canonical assets.
